task.description:
WF-03 Step 3c -- SECURITY GATE on the ISS-0109 implementation (commits 5556767 / 8367b4d on
feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821). Review the DIFF, not the developer's account of it:
`git diff 70736d5..HEAD -- test/` plus `git diff 70736d5..HEAD --stat`.

WHAT SHIPPED: one new test-only module test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (Letflow.TenantFixture)
and its adoption in exactly two test modules (test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs,
test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs). The gate-approved design is
lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md.

FIRST, RUN YOUR OWN SCOPE TEST AND STATE THE VERDICT EXPLICITLY. ELIXIR-DEV and the design
both assert this change touches NO tenant-data path -- no lib/ change at all, test-only code.
If that holds, most of INV-1..INV-8 are NOT-APPLICABLE and saying so per invariant is the
correct output; do not manufacture findings to justify the step. But VERIFY the premise
yourself rather than inheriting it: confirm from the diff that lib/ is genuinely untouched
(the design artefact itself is the only permitted lib/ path), and that the new module is
never referenced from shipped code and never enters lib/letflow/application.ex's supervision
tree.

THEN CHECK THE TWO INVARIANTS THE DESIGN ITSELF WROTE, because they are the reason this gate
runs at all on a test-only change -- this helper issues raw SQL against a multi-tenant
database:

INV-F-8 (design SS4): every query the helper issues is either (a) parameterized and scoped to
the single tenant/schema under test, or (b) a read of Postgres catalog metadata
(information_schema.schemata / information_schema.tables) filtered by table_schema = $1. No
value belonging to another tenant is ever read, logged, or returned. NO UNSCOPED CATALOG
ENUMERATION. Check every query in the new module against this, one by one. An unscoped
catalog read in a test helper is not harmless: it would make the failure-capture report leak
other tenants' schema names into logs, and this repo already has ISS-0111/GH#365 open for a
test that mutates shared tenant state globally.

INV-F-9 (design SS4): the ONLY raw-SQL identifier interpolation is DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS
"<name>" CASCADE and "<name>".schema_migrations, and <name> is ALWAYS the output of
TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 -- never a caller-supplied string. Everything else
is $1-parameterized. Verify by reading every interpolation site in the new file. This is the
same argument tenant_provisioning.ex:180-187 already makes for production; confirm the helper
actually earns it rather than merely claiming it.

ALSO CHECK, since it is a new logging surface: the teardown log line the helper emits at :info
carries schema name, tenant_id, schema_present_before_drop, test module and test name. Confirm
it contains NOTHING beyond the tenant under test -- no other tenant's identifiers, no
credentials, no connection string, no arbitrary exception text. A capture/logging helper is
exactly where a leak would be introduced casually and would then be copied into 39 more call
sites later (ISS-0112).

CONSTRAINTS: you gate, you do not edit. Report per-invariant verdicts (APPLIES PASS / APPLIES
FAIL / NOT-APPLICABLE with the reason). Toolchain here is Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against a
1.18.3-otp-27 pin (ISS-0106, filed, not yours) -- plain `mix compile` only, no
--warnings-as-errors, no `mix format`. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit scope verdict is stated, derived from the diff rather than from ELIXIR-DEV's claim: whether this change touches a tenant-data path, including confirmation that lib/ is untouched apart from the design artefact and that Letflow.TenantFixture is never referenced from shipped code or added to the supervision tree
A per-invariant verdict (APPLIES PASS / APPLIES FAIL / NOT-APPLICABLE with reason) is given for INV-1 through INV-8

INV-F-8 is checked query by query against the new module: every query is either tenant/schema-scoped and parameterized, or a catalog read filtered by table_schema = $1, with no unscoped catalog enumeration

INV-F-9 is checked interpolation site by interpolation site: the only raw-SQL identifier interpolation is the schema name from TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, never a caller-supplied string

The new teardown log line's contents are checked field by field and confirmed to carry nothing beyond the tenant under test -- no other tenant's identifiers, no credentials, no connection string, no arbitrary exception text
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated; on FAIL each finding names the specific line and the invariant it violates
